## 固定收益開篇主論

原油自本週高點回落，讓7月24日的美國公債市場獲得喘息。在此之前，油價驅動的重新定價已使殖利率急升，並讓聯準會7月升息重新成為市場議題。2年期殖利率下降1.5個基點至4.333%，5年期下降2.7個基點至4.426%，10年期回落1.6個基點至4.678%；30年期僅下降0.2個基點至5.159%，長期借款成本逼近近20年高點所形成的壓力大致未退。

這波小幅反彈並未扭轉全週走勢。5個交易日下來，2年期殖利率仍上升15.3個基點，10年期上升12.9個基點，30年期上升8.8個基點。布蘭特原油一度升破$100，最終收跌3.88%至$96.78，但全週仍上漲9.85%，一個月漲幅達25.56%。WTI下跌3.12%至$89.31，全週仍上漲8.27%。油價回落降低了立即再度收緊政策的壓力，卻未解答海灣航運受阻是否會讓能源價格維持高檔，進而擴散至更廣泛的通膨。

美債行情的組成正凸顯這項區別。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.4個基點至2.246%，降幅超過名目殖利率；10年期實質殖利率反而上升0.8個基點至2.432%。投資人調低油價飆升期間納入價格的部分通膨補償，卻仍要求更高的通膨調整後報酬。30年期殖利率幾乎未隨市場反彈，也顯示除了近期能源衝擊，財政供給以及日益增加的長天期公司債對資金的競爭仍不容忽視。

本交易日也沒有出現足以抵銷上述壓力的明確成長弱訊號。服務需求強勁，抵銷工廠生產降溫、供應延誤加劇與成本上升，使美國商業活動以8個月來最快速度擴張；新屋銷售亦增加。這些結果不足以迫使聯準會立即行動，但也幾乎沒有跡象顯示經濟活動惡化得足以讓決策者忽略能源與關稅可能帶來的通膨。市場仍認為7月28日至29日會議升息1碼的機率約為三分之一，並判斷9月採取行動的可能性高出許多。

風險資產呈現的是科技類股特有的回落，而非全面拋售。標普500指數近乎持平，漲幅不到0.05%，成分股中近360檔上漲；納斯達克100指數則下跌1.15%，費城半導體指數重挫4.25%。這項分歧使AI投資週期的融資需求與報酬不確定性持續居於信用市場討論核心。美元指數週五變動不大，但寫下一個月來最佳單週表現；黃金上漲0.52%至$4,067.60。

因此，本交易日雖以油價及美債名目殖利率回落作收，引發先前賣壓的各項力量卻未全面消退。通膨補償下降，實質殖利率仍高；短、中天期殖利率回落，長債卻幾乎未動；大盤股市守穩之際，半導體股票及AI相關信用債的壓力更加明顯。週末後續發展進一步壓低眼前的能源風險溢價，但事件發生在美國市場收盤後，降溫局勢能否持續仍未有定論。

## 油價回落僅限制、未扭轉美債跌勢

週五行情之前，衝突已在一週內由荷莫茲海峽蔓延至紅海，不僅威脅海灣能源的主要出口通道，也危及沙烏地阿拉伯用作部分替代方案的航線。布蘭特原油週四升破$100，曾推動10年期美債殖利率在週內升至4.71%、30年期升至5.19%。原油回落讓殖利率得以下降，但美債殖利率曲線仍保留對更大潛在能源衝擊的累積重新定價。

2年與10年期利差當日變動不大，報34.5個基點；2年與30年期利差則擴大1.3個基點至82.6個基點。長端這次表現略遜，有別於本週稍早由前端領跌的走勢。油價下降緩解了下一次政策決定的部分急迫性，但30年期債券幾乎沒有反彈，說明近期通膨補償下降仍不足以消除長端所含的期限、財政與供給溢價。

實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率的分化也指向相同結論。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.4個基點、實質殖利率卻上升0.8個基點，並非市場單純解除通膨恐慌時會出現的組合。油價反轉降低了預期價格壓力，但面對具韌性的經濟活動、不確定的聯準會政策，以及等待買方承接的大量主權與公司長天期債券，投資人仍要求可觀的實質補償。一個月來，10年期名目殖利率上升18個基點，實質殖利率上升15.3個基點，損益兩平通膨率僅上升2.7個基點。

價格趨穩之際，美債交易活動轉淡。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$8,031億，共336,929筆，面額較前一交易日減少30.6%。名目附息債交易量下降26.1%至$6,740億；超過3年至5年以及超過7年至10年兩個區段的周轉量都減少約四分之一。這些數字顯示市場在前一日調整後，雙向交易轉為清淡，並不能用來判斷客戶需求方向。

成長消息也限制了油價下跌所能帶動的債券漲幅。美國商業活動加速集中於服務業，製造業生產則降溫，供應延誤與成本同步增加。這項組合保留了聯準會難題的兩面：內需仍足以支撐經濟活動，但投入成本壓力、關稅與能源供應中斷可能使通膨無法順利回歸目標。新屋銷售上升也顯示，高房貸利率尚未造成住房需求毫無疑義的崩跌。

貿易政策也由宣布進入實施。先前的關稅遭最高法院推翻後，約60個經濟體的商品開始適用10%至12.5%的新關稅，取代即將到期的10%進口稅。智慧型手機與AI晶片等大型品類仍獲豁免；按金額計算，美國約半數進口商品不是從未納入，就是目前已被排除。豁免縮小了直接價格衝擊的幅度，但在能源成本已使通膨前景更加複雜之際，實際生效的關稅制度又增加一項供給面的不確定性。

跨資產收盤表現反映的是行情趨穩，而非市場相信衝擊已經結束。布蘭特原油即使當日下跌，仍接近$97；美元全週上漲0.5%；預期美債波動率本週一度升至5月以來最高。標普500指數收平掩蓋了科技股持續回落：納斯達克100指數自3月以來首次連續兩週下跌；半導體指數雖然當週上漲，一個月來仍跌逾12%。

週五固定收益市場收盤截點後，地緣政治情勢再度變化。美國在長達13天的軍事行動後暫停攻擊伊朗，伊朗表示已停止報復性攻擊，伊朗與阿曼官員也就荷莫茲海峽通航舉行會談。暫停行動並未使水道恢復通行，美國官員也表示軍事選項仍然存在；胡塞武裝的攻擊及沙烏地阿拉伯主導的回應，則讓紅海戰線持續活躍。

市場評估這段暫歇期間，布蘭特原油隨後一度重挫7.4%至$90以下，之後收斂跌幅。這段較晚出現的走勢不能解釋週五美債收盤，卻改變了下一交易日面對的首要問題。市場要檢驗的已不只是$100油價會否觸發進一步緊縮，而是這次暫停能否促成能源航線持久重開，抑或只是在一再復燃的衝突中形成又一次短暫中斷。

## AI舉債成為指數層級的信用議題

市場對AI支出的重新評估已由股市延伸至信用市場承接能力的直接考驗。與貝萊德有關的特殊目的公司計畫發行$123億債券，為Meta位於德州艾爾帕索的資料中心園區融資，收到約$200億認購需求。訂單簿約為擬發行規模的1.6倍，以投資等級債標準而言偏弱；這類借款人通常希望需求達發行量數倍，以爭取較有利的定價。

這批2048年到期債券預計於7月27日定價，利差約為10年期美債加287.5個基點。隨訂單累積，利差未見收窄，仍大致符合較早討論水準；相較另一筆為Meta資料中心融資、2049年到期的Beignet債券，利差也寬約40個基點。Beignet債券本身在7月已擴大逾50個基點，意味投資人採用的比較基準也正承受壓力。

這筆交易為一座預計可提供最高1吉瓦運算能力的園區融資。貝萊德旗下Global Infrastructure Management與HPS Investment Partners合計持有專案80%，Meta持有其餘20%。債務結構類似專案融資：由特殊目的公司發行，本金逐步攤還，並由Meta的租賃承諾支撐債務。這項安排可讓Meta在公司資產負債表外為基礎設施籌資，但無法消除投資人對租約、設施經濟效益及該運算能力長期價值的曝險。

市場反應疲弱之前，已有數筆大型科技債發行。Amazon在7月稍早發行$250億債券，訂單也僅約為發行額的1.6倍，遠低於今年美國投資等級債交易約4倍的平均水準。Meta在4月發行的$250億債券，定價利差寬於6個月前的$300億交易；一筆2046年到期的Meta債券自發行以來，利差已擴大約30個基點。Alphabet決定把2026年資本支出提高至最高$2,050億，則加深市場對舉債管線持續擴張的疑慮。

影響正超越任何單一交易。根據巴克萊資料，截至7月23日，6家最大科技公司占美國高評級公司債市場「存續期間乘以利差」風險的8.6%，高於6家最大銀行的7.3%。這項差距格外顯著，因為包括私募證券在內，超大規模雲端業者的債務僅占未償本金約4%，大型銀行債務的市值占比則約為9%。

到期結構解釋了大部分差異。科技公司大量在長端借款，為可能需要多年才能證明報酬的專案鎖定資金。過去12個月，超大規模雲端業者發行的債券約43%期限超過10年，相較之下，併購債務為24%，其他非金融企業發行則為23%。存續期間與利差風險相結合，使AI借款人對指數表現的影響遠高於其本金占比。

市場已開始重新定價這項風險。7月23日，科技業投資等級債利差約為89個基點，高於年初約76個基點。超大規模雲端業者的信用衍生品交易增加；部分長天期科技債即使維持較高的投資等級評等，交易利差也已接近BB級發行人。市場擔心的與其說是近期違約，不如說是集中度、供給，以及空前資本支出能否產生足夠報酬的不確定性。

巴克萊預估，超大規模雲端業者今年將在全球發行約$2,850億投資等級債。若此趨勢延續，投資人把更多資產負債表空間分配給長天期科技債後，可供其他借款人使用的承接能力就會下降，進而提高整體公司債指數中各類發行人所需提供的讓利。週五市場表現強化了這項區別：美國整體信用債基金近乎持平，但科技股與特定長天期AI融資明顯承壓。

因此，擬議中的Sopaipilla發行所決定的不只是一項專案的借款成本。在多筆大型交易已吸收市場需求後，這筆交易將顯示Meta租賃承諾與攤還結構，能否為規模$123億的長天期債券吸引足夠廣泛的訂單。之後的次級市場交易則將檢驗：當投資人用來比較的債券持續走弱時，初始利差是否提供充分補償。

在歐洲信用市場壓力較大的一端，英國地毯製造商Victoria的再融資程序又向前一步。HSBC在最後一刻加入後，公司表示債務重整已獲足夠支持；此前各方曾就一筆影響其2028年到期債券持有人的交易進行協商。公司也公布年度虧損£3.263億，較一年前的£2.758億擴大，主因為資產減記與減債成本。第一季銷量成長3%、營收增加7%，但再融資只是爭取到營運時間，並未消除消費需求疲弱、材料成本上升與債務即將到期所造成的損害。

## 歐洲權衡較溫和的預期、油價與財政供給

歐洲利率市場進入週末時，政策預期仍偏向緊縮，但最新資訊使再次升息不再像是理所當然。ECB調查顯示，歐元區消費者對未來1年的通膨預期由5月的3.5%降至6月的3%，3年期預期由2.9%微降至2.8%。調查期間為6月4日至29日，早於最近一波油價飆升，因此反映的是較溫和的起始狀態，而非民眾對新一輪能源衝擊的反應。

企業資料也指向壓力趨緩。企業向ECB表示，第二季售價漲幅低於預期，7月至9月可能略為放慢；企業預估2026年與2027年薪資分別成長2.5%與2.4%，低於去年的3.1%。專業預測者調查中的通膨預期變化不大，但2026年經濟成長預測幾乎減半。另一方面，歐元區民間部門活動仍升至5個月高點，使決策者面對較溫和的價格預期，卻看不到當前經濟活動明確惡化。

ECB在6月升息1碼後選擇維持利率不變，上述反差也形塑了多名官員隨後的發言。德國央行總裁Joachim Nagel為按兵不動辯護，並指出9月將有新數據與預測。奧地利央行總裁Martin Kocher則把下一次決定形容為升息與維持利率之間的選擇。他表示，油價的直接與間接影響已可見，但除了零星事例，尚無第二輪效應的確切證據，薪資將是一項重要檢驗。

法國央行總裁Emmanuel Moulin著重油價衝擊的規模與持續時間，尤其關注能源成本是否擴散至運輸與服務。愛沙尼亞央行總裁Ulo Kaasik同樣聚焦薪資，以及防止第二輪效應的必要性。立陶宛央行總裁Gediminas Simkus立場更明確，認為升息的可能性仍遠高於再次按兵不動。ECB首席經濟學家Philip Lane把能源供應中斷稱為中等規模衝擊，並表示9月政策調整將取決於油氣價格是否維持高檔，或荷莫茲海峽供應能否持久恢復。

這些立場構成有條件的緊縮傾向，而非政策承諾。消費者與企業預期在最近一輪衝突升級前已有改善，能源衝擊則尚未有足夠時間完整反映於數據。ECB的9月決定將取決於這項有利起點能否經受實際通膨、薪資設定與服務價格的考驗。由於6月已經升息，決策者有空間等待這些觀察結果，但公開發言顯示，他們對衝擊持續擴散的容忍度有限。

英國公債還承受額外的財政與供給負擔。油價回落帶動10年期英債殖利率週五下降約4個基點，但仍接近5.04%，創下2008年以來收盤連續高於5%的最長紀錄。投資人同時評估油價的通膨後果，以及首相Andy Burnham新政府的支出企圖。英國6月債務利息支出為£118億，幾乎與撥給地方政府的金額相當，說明在秋季預算公布完整政策內容前，目前的殖利率水準已對財政選擇形成制約。

英格蘭銀行的資產負債表計畫另是一項久期供給來源。央行仍持有£4,920億英國公債，除讓債券到期不再投資外，也一直主動出售債券。本量化緊縮年度的主動出售金額為£210億。大額債券到期使資產負債表整體得以縮減£700億，但明年到期金額將大幅下降；若要從10月起維持目前的整體縮表速度，主動出售規模必須倍增至約£400億。

市場參與者平均預期，英格蘭銀行會把主動出售規模維持在£200億附近，並將全年總縮表額降至約£500億。央行先前估計量化緊縮已使10年期英債殖利率增加15至25個基點，較新的內部研究則認為最高影響接近40個基點。總裁Andrew Bailey仍主張，央行必須重建資產負債表的政策操作空間，以因應未來危機；但退休基金需求減弱、政府發債及已然偏高的長端殖利率，都使出售速度更具影響力。

英格蘭銀行將在7月30日利率決策時公布更新分析，並於9月作出最終縮表決定。利率與資產負債表決策彼此相關，卻是兩個不同問題。維持政策利率不變不會消除主動出售英債的供給效應；放慢出售速度，也不能回答輸入型能源通膨是否需要日後升息。

## 日本長端與中國貸款基準分歧

在亞洲，日本債市最明顯地反映高能源價格、日圓疲弱及貨幣政策正常化速度不確定所造成的壓力。40年期日本公債殖利率上升10個基點至4.01%，逐步逼近5月創下的4.355%紀錄；5年期殖利率則升至該年期自2000年推出以來最高。這波走勢延續全球長天期債券賣壓，也反映日本市場特有的疑慮：日本央行收緊政策的步伐可能太慢，無法遏制輸入型通膨。

日圓一度貶至1美元兌163.99日圓，創1986年以來最低，並可能寫下5月以來最大單週跌幅。截至7月21日，避險基金把受惠於日圓進一步貶值的部位增至114,030口，價值約$87億。干預警告未能帶來持久支撐，因為較高的美債殖利率、龐大的政策利差及日本對進口能源的依賴仍彼此強化。

據報日本央行官員願意考慮比經濟學家預期時程更快升息，但市場仍普遍預期7月31日會議將把政策利率維持在1%。受訪經濟學家中有半數預期下一次行動在12月，交換市場則反映年底前約32個基點的緊縮幅度。兩者的落差使本次會議的溝通格外重要：即使不立即升息，偏鷹派的按兵不動也可能讓市場定價的升息時程提前。

財政政策也在長端增加壓力。首相高市早苗政府批准一項包含積極投資與國防目標的經濟計畫，卻未解決可能調降食品消費稅所需的融資問題。資金細節付之闕如，無法安撫已對債務軌跡抱持疑慮的投資人。日圓走弱又會推高進口成本，使政策困境更加複雜，並強化採取貨幣行動的理由；這類行動本身也可能推升日本短天期殖利率。

中國的方向相反，開始嘗試把較低的貨幣市場資金成本更直接傳導至銀行貸款。中國工商銀行、招商銀行及上海浦東發展銀行海口分行首次發放與銀行間附買回利率連結的貸款，不再完全依賴貸款市場報價利率（LPR）。

中國工商銀行向一家外資企業提供人民幣7,670萬元、期限1年的貸款，利率連結隔夜附買回利率。上海浦東發展銀行向一家國有企業提供人民幣700萬元貸款，招商銀行的交易規模據報為人民幣800萬元；後兩家銀行均未揭露基準利率的天期。

這些交易規模雖小，基準的轉變卻相當重要。LPR自2019年起一直是銀行貸款的主要參考利率，若政策利率未作調整，LPR很少變動。即使債券殖利率與銀行間融資成本下降，LPR自中國人民銀行2025年5月上次調降後便維持不變。3月發放的貸款中，近半數的定價低於LPR，遠高於2019年的16%，顯示官方基準與實際融資環境日益脫節。

與附買回利率連結的貸款，可在銀行不必放棄LPR的情況下，改善每日流動性條件向借款成本的傳導。此前，中國人民銀行已推出新的隔夜流動性工具，並公開支持更多元的基準制度。這項發展屬於貨幣政策傳導改革，而非大規模刺激措施；但在國內信貸需求疲弱、投資放緩之際，既有寬鬆措施能否更有效抵達借款人，正面臨更大壓力。

預計數日內召開的中共中央政治局會議，將決定北京是否在調整傳導機制的同時加快財政執行。截至6月底，今年新增政府債券額度僅使用43%，下半年尚餘人民幣6.8兆元；這比去年同期剩餘額度多人民幣1.3兆元，相當於下半年GDP約1.8%。經濟學家普遍預期，官員將加速執行現有支出，而非重演2024年的大幅政策轉向。

## 出口路線化為資本計畫，海灣融資擴張

區域能源運輸路線受阻，不只影響每日油價，也開始重塑主權借款。今年海灣發行人已售出創紀錄的$1,120億債券；沙烏地阿拉伯、科威特、阿拉伯聯合大公國及卡達正討論為港口、管線與道路取得更多融資，以降低對荷莫茲海峽的依賴。

潛在專案包括在紅海與阿曼灣興建新碼頭、修復老舊管線及擴建陸路運輸。沙烏地阿拉伯一直在恢復通往延布的東西向管線，阿聯也討論興建可消除荷莫茲海峽依賴的港口與管線。這些專案旨在減少對單一咽喉點的曝險，但胡塞武裝攻擊與沙烏地阿拉伯有關的油輪，也顯示紅海替代航線自有其安全風險。

新增供給目前仍有買方承接。科威特本週發行$60億債券，即使其石油出口嚴重受阻，認購金額仍超過發行量2倍。沙烏地阿拉伯、阿布達比及卡達今年稍早的發行也獲得強勁需求。龐大外匯存底與高信用評等，使這些主權發行人即使面臨衝突，仍保有可用的融資能力。

不過，投資人已開始對地緣政治曝險與潛在發債供給同時要求補償。2054年到期的阿布達比債券利差約為美債加82個基點，高於1月的53個基點。利差擴大既反映衝突，也反映額外專案需要更多舉債的預期。不同地理位置之間的差異可能更加重要：沙烏地阿拉伯、阿聯與阿曼擁有較多替代路線，科威特、巴林及卡達則較少；然而，一旦戰爭範圍擴大，沒有任何繞行路線可以不受波及。

馬來西亞重返美元債市場，則顯示能源衝擊也正改變海灣以外國家的財政需求。該國透過5年來首次發行的美元伊斯蘭債券籌得$15億，包括一筆2032年4月到期、殖利率4.612%的$8.5億債券，以及一筆2036年7月到期、殖利率4.949%的$6.5億債券。

訂單達發行量4.7倍，使馬來西亞得以將定價較初步指引收窄30個基點，並創下該國全球伊斯蘭債券歷來最窄利差。強勁需求的背景是第二季經濟年增5.8%，由國內消費、半導體與AI投資，以及電子產品出口支撐。

這次融資之際，馬來西亞也警告燃料補貼支出可能破壞本年度赤字目標。首相安華估計，若現行價格延續，汽油與柴油補貼可能達400億令吉，約合$98億，超過2026年預算所編列150億令吉的2倍。伊斯蘭債券所得用於基礎設施及償還既有債務，並非完全指定補貼用途，但在政府10月初提出下一份預算前，這筆交易仍強化了政府流動性。

綜合而言，海灣與馬來西亞的發債顯示，即使能源與地緣政治壓力升高，主權發行人仍可進入市場。差別在於舉債原因：海灣產油國考慮透過債務建立更具韌性的出口能力；馬來西亞對進口油價敏感的補貼制度則推高財政成本。即使目前投資需求仍強，兩者都使衝突與未來債券供給產生連結。

## 市場前瞻意義

7月28日至29日的FOMC會議，是美國利率眼前的首要考驗。油價飆升後，期貨市場認為升息1碼的機率約為35%至37%，幾乎所有受訪經濟學家則預期聯準會維持利率不變。達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan與克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack主張，在雙重使命中，通膨是更迫切的問題，兩人可能反對按兵不動。副主席Philip Jefferson表示，若通膨持續未能降溫，便可能有理由重新考慮政策立場；其他官員則傾向等待更多證據。

若聯準會按兵不動，記者會將決定9月升息能否繼續成為市場基準情境。主席Kevin Warsh降低對前瞻指引的依賴，使可能結果的分布較以往類似會議更廣。升息將使市場轉向較高的終端利率預期，並可能令殖利率曲線趨平；若維持利率不變卻未清楚說明，投資人可能認為聯準會容忍更大的通膨風險，讓長端殖利率繼續承壓。

隨後公布的美國數據將同時檢驗這項決定的兩面。第二季GDP預計在消費者與企業投資支持下，以年率成長2.1%。6月個人消費與通膨數據則預計反映最近一輪衝突升級前較低的汽油價格。決策者判斷衝擊屬於暫時還是逐漸持久化時，這種落後回顧的能源比較與當前油價之間的差異將相當重要。

地緣政治走向仍可能比經濟數據更早改變政策盤算。若美國與伊朗暫停軍事行動的局面得以持續、阿曼會談取得進展，且荷莫茲海峽恢復通航，近期通膨溢價將會下降。若攻擊重啟，或荷莫茲海峽與紅海均持續受阻，原油價格、運費與保險成本將持續面臨上漲壓力。布蘭特原油稍後跌破$90，顯示局勢降溫可以多快扭轉政策定價；但航道尚未重開，意味改善仍有條件。

Sopaipilla預計於7月27日定價，是近期最清楚的信用市場承接能力考驗。投資人將判斷，在訂單簿僅為1.6倍的情況下，約287.5個基點的利差與Meta租賃承諾，是否足以支撐$123億交易。其後的次級市場表現也將與7月29日Microsoft及Meta、7月30日Apple及Amazon的財報一併受到關注。AI支出若進一步增加，將強化更多長天期供給即將出現的預期；若有證據顯示報酬改善，則有助區分融資規模擴張與信用惡化。

英格蘭銀行7月30日會議必須同時處理油價衝擊與量化緊縮。市場普遍預期政策利率不變，但少數決策者可能支持升息。當維持目前整體縮表速度可能要求主動出售規模倍增時，央行更新後的資產負債表分析將顯示官員是否準備減少主動出售英國公債。對長端而言，量化緊縮訊號的重要性可能不亞於利率表決。

日本央行將於7月31日接續登場。市場預期政策利率維持1%，但日圓接近40年低點、40年期殖利率高於4%，已提高央行繼續傳達耐心訊息的代價。央行對匯率傳導、能源價格及下次升息時點的指引，將決定市場是否維持年底前緊縮約32個基點的預期，或向經濟學家較為偏好的12月時程靠攏。

歐元區GDP與通膨數據將開始為ECB 9月10日的決定建立依據。經濟學家預期第二季成長0.2%、7月通膨率為2.9%；這些預測將呈現具韌性的經濟活動與加快的物價漲幅，但更關鍵的問題是能源成本是否滲入服務、薪資及中期預期。6月消費者預期下降，為ECB提供有利的比較起點，卻無法回答家庭與企業如何回應7月衝擊。

中國的中共中央政治局會議將檢驗決策者是否加快發行剩餘人民幣6.8兆元債券，並改善既有財政支持的落實速度。加快支出時程可在不重演2024年刺激方案的情況下支持經濟活動。首批與附買回利率連結的銀行貸款還帶來另一項問題：當信貸需求本身依然疲弱時，更具彈性的基準能否把銀行間低利率傳導至實體經濟。

綜觀上述事件，債券市場正把暫時性的價格壓力緩解，與持續存在的融資壓力區分開來。正如週五損益兩平通膨率下降所顯示，油價走低可以削減部分近期通膨補償；但單靠油價下降，無法降低偏高的實質殖利率、吸收主權及AI相關的長天期債券供給，也不能化解使美國、英國與日本長端殖利率居高不下的財政及政策限制。

overall_summary.session_narrative:
原油自本週高點回落，帶動美國公債小幅上漲。2年期殖利率下降1.5個基點至4.333%，5年期下降2.7個基點至4.426%，10年期回落1.6個基點至4.678%；30年期僅下降0.2個基點至5.159%。布蘭特原油一度升破$100，最終收跌3.88%至$96.78，降低眼前的通膨壓力，卻未扭轉本週美債殖利率與油價大幅上升的走勢。

行情組成說明了為何這次喘息仍然有限。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2.4個基點至2.246%，10年期實質殖利率卻上升0.8個基點至2.432%。投資人削減部分與油價有關的通膨補償，同時仍要求偏高的通膨調整後報酬；財政供給與不斷增加的公司長天期債券，也繼續對長債形成壓力。

服務業抵銷製造業走弱，使美國商業活動以8個月來最快速度擴張，新屋銷售也上升。數據幾乎沒有顯示經濟成長弱到足以讓聯準會忽略能源與關稅風險。整體股市持穩，但納斯達克100指數與半導體股票下跌；長天期AI融資需求疲弱，凸顯投資等級信用市場日益加重的供給與集中度壓力。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries steadied on July 24 as crude retreated from the week’s peak, giving the market a modest reprieve after an oil-driven repricing had lifted yields sharply and brought a Federal Reserve increase back into the July discussion. The 2-year yield declined 1.5 basis points to 4.333%, the 5-year fell 2.7 basis points to 4.426%, and the 10-year eased 1.6 basis points to 4.678%. The 30-year yield slipped just 0.2 basis point to 5.159%, preserving most of the pressure that had taken long borrowing costs toward their highest levels in almost 2 decades.

The small rally did not reverse the week’s move. The 2-year yield remained 15.3 basis points higher over 5 sessions, the 10-year was up 12.9 basis points and the 30-year had risen 8.8 basis points. Brent settled 3.88% lower at $96.78 after briefly trading above $100, but was still 9.85% higher over the week and 25.56% higher over a month. WTI fell 3.12% to $89.31, leaving it 8.27% higher over the week. The decline in crude reduced the immediate pressure for another round of policy tightening without resolving whether disrupted Gulf shipping will keep energy prices elevated long enough to enter broader inflation.

The composition of the Treasury move underscored that distinction. The 10-year breakeven rate fell 2.4 basis points to 2.246%, accounting for more than the decline in the nominal yield, while the 10-year real yield increased 0.8 basis point to 2.432%. Investors marked down some of the inflation compensation embedded during the oil surge but continued to demand a higher inflation-adjusted return. The 30-year yield’s resistance to the rally also left fiscal supply and competition from a growing volume of long-dated corporate borrowing relevant alongside the near-term energy shock.

The session brought no decisive growth offset. U.S. business activity expanded at its fastest pace in 8 months as strong demand for services outweighed cooling factory production, longer supply delays and rising costs. New-home sales also increased. Those results did not compel an immediate Fed move, but they offered little indication that activity was deteriorating fast enough to make policymakers disregard prospective inflation from energy and tariffs. Markets continued to assign roughly a one-third probability to a quarter-point increase at the July 28–29 meeting and treated a September move as substantially more likely.

Risk assets showed a technology-specific retreat rather than a generalized liquidation. The S&P 500 was effectively unchanged, rising less than 0.05%, and nearly 360 of its constituents advanced. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.15%, however, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.25%. The divergence kept the financing demands and uncertain returns of the artificial-intelligence investment cycle near the center of the credit-market discussion. The dollar index was little changed on Friday but completed its best week in a month, while gold rose 0.52% to $4,067.60.

The session therefore ended with relief in oil and nominal Treasury yields but not a broad retreat from the forces that produced the selloff. Inflation compensation eased, yet real yields remained firm; short and intermediate yields declined, yet the long bond barely moved; and broad equities held up even as semiconductor shares and AI-linked credit showed greater strain. Subsequent weekend developments reduced the immediate energy premium further, but they arrived after the completed U.S. close and left the durability of any de-escalation unresolved.

## Oil Relief Limits, Rather Than Reverses, the Treasury Selloff

Friday’s price action followed a week in which the conflict spread from the Strait of Hormuz to the Red Sea, threatening both the principal outlet for Gulf energy and the route Saudi Arabia had been using as a partial alternative. Brent’s move above $100 on Thursday had helped push the 10-year Treasury yield as high as 4.71% during the week and the 30-year to 5.19%. The pullback in crude allowed yields to ease, but the Treasury curve retained the cumulative effects of a much larger prospective energy shock.

The 2s10s curve was little changed on the day at 34.5 basis points, while 2s30s steepened 1.3 basis points to 82.6 basis points. That modest long-end underperformance differed from the front-end-led selloff earlier in the week. Lower crude reduced some of the urgency around the next policy decision, but the near absence of a 30-year rally showed that easing near-term inflation compensation was insufficient to remove the term, fiscal and supply premium embedded at the long end.

The real-yield and breakeven split made the same point from another direction. A 2.4-basis-point fall in 10-year breakevens alongside a 0.8-basis-point increase in real yields is not the configuration of a market simply unwinding an inflation scare. It indicates that the reversal in oil reduced expected price pressure while investors still required substantial real compensation for resilient activity, uncertain Fed policy and the volume of sovereign and corporate duration seeking buyers. Over a month, the 10-year nominal yield was 18 basis points higher, the real yield had risen 15.3 basis points and the breakeven only 2.7 basis points.

Treasury trading activity was lighter as prices stabilized. FINRA recorded $803.1 billion of par activity across 336,929 trades, 30.6% less par volume than the previous session. Nominal-coupon activity fell 26.1% to $674 billion. Turnover declined by roughly a quarter in both the greater-than-3-year through 5-year sector and the greater-than-7-year through 10-year sector. The figures describe a quieter two-way market after the previous day’s adjustment; they do not identify the direction of customer demand.

The growth news helped prevent the oil decline from becoming a larger duration rally. The acceleration in U.S. business activity was concentrated in services, while manufacturing production cooled and supply delays and costs increased. That mixture preserved both sides of the Fed’s problem: domestic demand remained capable of supporting activity, but the combination of input pressure, tariffs and energy disruption could keep inflation from returning smoothly toward target. Rising new-home sales added evidence that high mortgage rates had not produced an unambiguous collapse in housing demand.

Trade policy also moved from announcement to operation. New duties of 10% to 12.5% took effect on goods from about 60 economies, replacing an expiring 10% import tax after earlier levies were struck down by the Supreme Court. Large categories including smartphones and AI chips remained exempt, and roughly half of U.S. imports by value had either never been covered or were now excluded. The carve-outs limit the scale of the direct price impulse, but the effective tariff regime adds another supply-side uncertainty at a time when energy costs are already complicating the inflation outlook.

The cross-asset close reflected stabilization rather than confidence that the shock had passed. Brent remained near $97 even after its daily decline, the dollar completed a 0.5% weekly gain, and expected Treasury volatility had reached its highest level since May during the week. The S&P 500’s flat close concealed a continued retreat in technology: the Nasdaq 100 completed a second consecutive weekly decline for the first time since March, and the semiconductor index was down more than 12% over a month despite its positive weekly performance.

After Friday’s fixed-income cutoff, the geopolitical picture shifted again. The U.S. paused strikes against Iran after a 13-day campaign, Iran said it had halted retaliatory attacks, and Iranian and Omani officials held talks concerning navigation through Hormuz. The pause did not reopen the waterway, and U.S. officials said military options remained available. Houthi attacks and Saudi-led responses also kept the Red Sea front active.

Brent subsequently fell as much as 7.4% to below $90 before paring the decline as markets assessed the lull. That later move cannot explain Friday’s Treasury close, but it changes the immediate question facing the next session. The test is no longer only whether $100 oil produces additional tightening; it is whether the pause develops into a durable reopening of energy routes or merely creates another temporary interruption in a conflict that has repeatedly resumed.

## AI Borrowing Becomes an Index-Level Credit Issue

The reassessment of AI spending moved from equities into a more direct test of credit-market capacity. A BlackRock-linked special-purpose vehicle received about $20 billion of demand for a planned $12.3 billion bond sale financing a Meta data-center campus in El Paso, Texas. An orderbook of roughly 1.6 times the proposed size was weak by investment-grade standards, where borrowers generally seek demand several times the amount offered to improve pricing.

The notes, due in 2048, were expected to price on July 27 at a spread near 287.5 basis points over 10-year Treasuries. That level remained broadly in line with earlier discussions rather than tightening as the orderbook developed. It was also around 40 basis points wider than a Beignet note due in 2049 that financed another Meta data center. The Beignet security had itself widened by more than 50 basis points during July, indicating that the comparison point was already under pressure.

The transaction finances a campus expected to provide as much as 1 gigawatt of computing capacity. BlackRock subsidiaries Global Infrastructure Management and HPS Investment Partners own 80% of the project, with Meta holding the remaining 20%. The debt resembles project finance: the issuer is a special-purpose vehicle, principal is repaid gradually and Meta’s lease commitments support the obligations. The structure allows Meta to fund infrastructure outside its corporate balance sheet, but it does not eliminate investors’ exposure to the lease, the facility’s economics or the long-term value of the capacity.

The weak reception follows several large technology offerings. Amazon’s $25 billion sale earlier in July drew orders equal to only about 1.6 times the amount issued, far below the roughly four-times average for U.S. investment-grade deals this year. Meta’s own $25 billion April offering priced at wider spreads than its $30 billion transaction 6 months earlier, and a Meta note due in 2046 had widened about 30 basis points since issuance. Alphabet’s decision to lift 2026 capital spending to as much as $205 billion added concern that the borrowing pipeline will continue expanding.

The consequences are becoming larger than any single deal. The 6 biggest technology companies represented 8.6% of the duration-times-spread risk in the U.S. high-grade corporate market as of July 23, according to Barclays, exceeding the 7.3% contribution of the 6 largest banks. That is striking because hyperscaler debt accounted for only about 4% of outstanding principal, including privately placed securities, compared with roughly 9% of market value for the large banks.

Maturity explains much of the difference. Technology companies are borrowing heavily at the long end to lock in capital for projects whose returns may take years to establish. About 43% of hyperscaler issuance during the past 12 months had maturities longer than 10 years, compared with 24% of merger-and-acquisition debt and 23% of other non-financial issuance. The resulting combination of duration and spread risk gives AI borrowers an influence on index performance disproportionate to their share of principal.

That risk is already being repriced. Technology investment-grade spreads were about 89 basis points on July 23, up from roughly 76 basis points at the start of the year. Credit-derivative activity in hyperscaler names had increased, while some long-dated technology bonds were trading at spreads near those of BB-rated issuers despite retaining high investment-grade ratings. The concern is less immediate default than concentration, supply and uncertainty over the return generated by unprecedented capital spending.

Barclays expects hyperscalers to issue about $285 billion of investment-grade debt globally this year. If that trajectory continues, buyers allocating more balance sheet to long technology debt will have less capacity for other borrowers, raising the concessions needed across the wider corporate index. Friday’s market performance reinforced that distinction: broad U.S. credit funds were nearly unchanged, but technology shares and specific long-dated AI financings were under visible pressure.

The planned Sopaipilla sale will therefore set more than a project-specific borrowing cost. It will show whether a Meta lease and amortizing structure can produce a sufficiently broad orderbook for a $12.3 billion, long-maturity transaction after several large deals have already absorbed demand. Secondary trading will then establish whether the initial spread provides enough compensation when the comparable bonds against which investors are judging the issue continue to weaken.

At the stressed end of European credit, Victoria completed another step in its refinancing process. The British carpetmaker said it had obtained sufficient support for its debt restructuring after HSBC joined at the last minute. That followed negotiations over a transaction affecting holders of its 2028 notes. The company also reported a £326.3 million annual loss, wider than £275.8 million a year earlier, largely because of writedowns and debt-reduction costs. First-quarter volumes rose 3% and revenue 7%, but the refinancing has bought operating time rather than erased the damage from weak consumer demand, higher material costs and looming maturities.

## Europe Weighs Softer Expectations Against Oil and Fiscal Supply

European rates entered the weekend with policy expectations still tilted toward tightening, but fresh information complicated the case for treating another increase as automatic. An ECB survey showed that euro-area consumers’ 1-year inflation expectations fell to 3% in June from 3.5% in May, while the 3-year measure slipped to 2.8% from 2.9%. The survey ran from June 4 through June 29, before the latest oil surge, so it describes a more benign starting point rather than the public’s response to the renewed energy shock.

Corporate evidence also pointed toward moderation. Businesses told the ECB that selling prices increased less than expected in Q2 and were likely to slow slightly from July through September. They anticipated wage growth of 2.5% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027, down from 3.1% last year. A survey of professional forecasters showed little change in inflation expectations but almost halved its forecast for 2026 economic growth. Euro-area private-sector activity nevertheless rose to a 5-month high, leaving policymakers with softer price expectations but no clear deterioration in current activity.

The contrast shaped a series of ECB interventions after the bank held rates following June’s quarter-point increase. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel defended the hold and said September would bring new data and projections. Austrian central-bank Governor Martin Kocher described the coming decision as a choice between a hike and a hold. He said direct and indirect effects from oil were visible but there was no hard evidence of second-round effects beyond anecdotes, with wages an important test.

Bank of France Governor Emmanuel Moulin emphasized the size and duration of the oil shock, particularly whether energy costs spread into transport and services. Estonia’s Ulo Kaasik similarly focused on wages and the need to prevent second-round effects. Lithuania’s Gediminas Simkus was more explicit, saying an increase remained much more likely than another hold. Chief Economist Philip Lane called the energy disruption a medium-sized shock and said the September calibration would depend on whether oil and gas remained high or supplies through Hormuz reopened durably.

Those positions form a conditional tightening bias rather than a promise. Consumer and corporate expectations had improved before the latest escalation, while the energy shock had not yet had time to appear fully in the data. The ECB’s September decision will turn on whether that favorable starting point survives through realized inflation, wage setting and services prices. The region’s policymakers have room to wait for those observations because they already raised rates in June, but the public comments show limited tolerance for a persistent broadening of the shock.

British gilts carried an additional fiscal and supply burden. The 10-year gilt yield declined about 4 basis points on Friday as oil eased, but remained near 5.04%, completing its longest sequence of closes above 5% since 2008. Investors were assessing both the inflation consequences of oil and the spending ambitions of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s new government. The U.K. spent £11.8 billion servicing its debt in June, almost as much as it transferred to local governments, illustrating how yields at these levels constrain fiscal choices before the autumn budget supplies complete policy terms.

The Bank of England’s balance-sheet plans add a separate source of duration. It still holds £492 billion of gilts and has been actively selling bonds as well as allowing maturities to run off. Active sales total £21 billion in the current quantitative-tightening year. Large redemptions allow the overall balance sheet to shrink by £70 billion, but maturities fall sharply next year; maintaining the current total pace from October would require active sales to double to about £40 billion.

Market participants on average expect the BOE to keep active sales near £20 billion and reduce total annual runoff to roughly £50 billion. The bank previously estimated that quantitative tightening had added 15 to 25 basis points to 10-year gilt yields, while more recent staff research put the peak effect near 40 basis points. Governor Andrew Bailey continues to argue that the balance sheet must be rebuilt as policy capacity for a future crisis, but fading pension demand, government issuance and already-high long yields make the pace of sales more consequential.

The BOE will publish updated analysis alongside its July 30 rate decision, ahead of a final runoff decision in September. The interest-rate and balance-sheet choices are related but distinct. Holding the policy rate would not remove the supply effect of active gilt sales, while slowing those sales would not settle whether imported energy inflation requires a later rate increase.

## Japan’s Long End and China’s Loan Benchmarks Diverge

Japan’s bond market remained the clearest Asian expression of the pressure created by expensive energy, a weak currency and uncertainty over the pace of monetary normalization. The 40-year government-bond yield rose 10 basis points to 4.01%, moving toward its May record of 4.355%. The 5-year yield reached its highest level since the maturity was introduced in 2000. The move extended the global duration selloff but also reflected a specifically Japanese concern that the Bank of Japan is moving too slowly to contain imported inflation.

The yen touched 163.99 per dollar, its weakest level since 1986, and was headed for its largest weekly loss since May. Hedge funds increased positions benefiting from further yen depreciation to 114,030 contracts, worth about $8.7 billion, as of July 21. Intervention warnings produced little lasting support because higher U.S. yields, the wide policy-rate differential and Japan’s dependence on imported energy continued to reinforce one another.

BOJ officials were reported to be open to raising rates faster than the timetable favored by economists, but the July 31 meeting is still widely expected to leave the 1% policy rate unchanged. Half the economists surveyed expected the next move in December, while swaps priced about 32 basis points of tightening through year-end. The conflict between those expectations gives the meeting’s communication unusual importance: a hawkish hold could accelerate the priced path even without an immediate increase.

Fiscal policy is adding pressure at the long end. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s government approved an economic plan with ambitious investment and defense goals while leaving the financing of a likely food sales-tax cut unresolved. The absence of detailed funding offered little comfort to investors already questioning the debt trajectory. A weaker yen then compounds the policy difficulty by raising import costs and strengthening the case for monetary action that could itself lift shorter Japanese yields.

China moved in the opposite direction by experimenting with a more direct transmission of lower money-market funding costs into bank lending. Industrial & Commercial Bank of China, China Merchants Bank and Shanghai Pudong Development Bank’s Haikou branch issued their first loans linked to interbank repo rates rather than relying exclusively on the loan prime rate.

ICBC extended a 76.7 million-yuan, 1-year loan to a foreign company linked to the overnight repo rate. Shanghai Pudong Development Bank provided 7 million yuan to a state-owned enterprise, while China Merchants Bank’s transaction was reported at 8 million yuan. The latter 2 banks did not disclose the benchmark tenor.

The transactions are small, but the benchmark change is important. The LPR has been the principal reference for bank loans since 2019 and has rarely moved without an adjustment in the policy rate. It has been unchanged since the People’s Bank of China’s last reduction in May 2025 even as bond yields and interbank funding costs declined. Nearly half of loans issued in March were priced below the LPR, up from 16% in 2019, indicating that the official reference was increasingly detached from actual financing conditions.

Repo-linked lending could improve the pass-through from daily liquidity conditions to borrowing costs without requiring banks to abandon the LPR. It follows the PBOC’s introduction of a new overnight liquidity tool and its public support for a more diversified benchmark system. The development is a monetary-transmission reform rather than a large stimulus measure, but it arrives as weak domestic credit demand and slowing investment increase pressure for existing easing to reach borrowers more efficiently.

The Politburo meeting expected within days will determine whether Beijing pairs that transmission change with faster fiscal execution. Only 43% of the year’s new government-bond quota had been used by the end of June, leaving 6.8 trillion yuan for H2. That was 1.3 trillion yuan more than the comparable remaining quota last year and equal to about 1.8% of H2 GDP. Economists broadly expected officials to accelerate existing spending rather than repeat the large policy pivot of 2024.

## Gulf Funding Expands as Export Routes Become Capital Projects

The disruption of regional energy routes is beginning to reshape sovereign borrowing as well as daily oil prices. Gulf issuers had sold a record $112 billion of debt this year, and Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar were discussing additional financing for ports, pipelines and roads that could reduce dependence on the Strait of Hormuz.

Potential projects include new terminals on the Red Sea and Gulf of Oman, repairs to aging pipelines and expanded overland transport. Saudi Arabia has been reviving its east-west pipeline to Yanbu, while the UAE has discussed ports and pipelines intended to eliminate reliance on Hormuz. The projects are designed to reduce exposure to one chokepoint, but Houthi attacks on Saudi-linked tankers showed that alternative Red Sea routes carry their own security risk.

The supply is still finding buyers. Kuwait’s $6 billion sale during the week drew orders exceeding twice the amount offered even as its oil exports were severely disrupted. Saudi Arabia, Abu Dhabi and Qatar had also received robust demand earlier in the year. Large foreign-exchange reserves and high ratings give these sovereigns financing capacity that remains available despite the conflict.

Investors are nevertheless beginning to charge for both geopolitical exposure and prospective issuance. Abu Dhabi bonds due in 2054 traded about 82 basis points over Treasuries, compared with 53 basis points in January. The widening reflects the conflict as well as expectations that additional projects will require more debt. Geographic differences may become more important: Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Oman have greater access to alternative routes than Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar, though no bypass is insulated from a wider war.

Malaysia’s return to the dollar market illustrated how the energy shock is also altering fiscal needs outside the Gulf. The sovereign raised $1.5 billion through its first dollar sukuk sale in 5 years. It sold an $850 million note due in April 2032 at a 4.612% yield and a $650 million tranche due in July 2036 at 4.949%.

Orders reached 4.7 times the amount offered, allowing Malaysia to tighten pricing by 30 basis points from initial indications and achieve its narrowest-ever spreads for a global sukuk. The demand reflected an economy that grew 5.8% from a year earlier in Q2, supported by domestic consumption, semiconductor and AI investment, and electronics exports.

The financing also came as Malaysia warned that its fuel-subsidy bill could undermine the year’s deficit target. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim estimated that petrol and diesel support could reach 40 billion ringgit, or $9.8 billion, if prevailing prices persisted. That is more than twice the 15 billion ringgit allocated in the 2026 budget. The sukuk funds infrastructure and refinances existing obligations rather than being assigned solely to subsidies, but the transaction strengthens the government’s liquidity before it presents its next budget in early October.

Together, Gulf and Malaysian issuance showed that sovereign market access remained open despite energy and geopolitical stress. The distinction was in the reason for borrowing: Gulf producers are considering debt to construct export resilience, while an oil-import-sensitive subsidy system is raising Malaysia’s fiscal cost. Both link the conflict to future bond supply even when current investor demand remains strong.

## Forward Market Significance

The July 28–29 FOMC meeting is the immediate U.S. rates test. Futures assigned roughly a 35% to 37% probability to a quarter-point increase after oil’s surge, while virtually all economists surveyed expected the Fed to hold. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack have argued that inflation is the more pressing mandate concern and could dissent from an unchanged decision. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson has indicated that a continued failure of inflation to cool could justify reconsidering the stance, while other officials favor waiting for more evidence.

A hold would leave the press conference to determine whether September remains the market’s base case. Chair Kevin Warsh’s reduced reliance on advance guidance has made the distribution of outcomes wider than before comparable meetings. A hike would shift expectations toward a higher terminal rate and could flatten the curve. A poorly explained hold could instead leave long yields exposed if investors conclude that the Fed is tolerating a larger inflation risk.

The subsequent U.S. data will test both sides of that decision. Q2 GDP is expected to show annualized growth of 2.1%, supported by consumers and business investment. June personal-consumption and inflation figures are expected to reflect lower gasoline prices that preceded the latest conflict escalation. The distinction between those backward-looking energy comparisons and current oil prices will matter when policymakers assess whether the shock is temporary or becoming persistent.

The geopolitical path remains capable of changing that calculation before the data do. A durable U.S.-Iran pause, progress in the Oman talks and restored traffic through Hormuz would reduce the near-term inflation premium. Renewed strikes or sustained disruption in both Hormuz and the Red Sea would keep pressure on crude, freight and insurance. The later fall in Brent below $90 shows how quickly policy pricing can reverse on de-escalation, but the lack of a reopened waterway leaves the improvement conditional.

Sopaipilla’s expected July 27 pricing is the clearest near-term credit-capacity test. Investors will judge whether a spread near 287.5 basis points and Meta’s lease commitments are sufficient for a $12.3 billion deal with only a 1.6-times orderbook. Its secondary performance will matter alongside earnings from Microsoft and Meta on July 29 and Apple and Amazon on July 30. Additional increases in AI spending would reinforce the prospect of more long-dated supply; evidence of improving returns could help distinguish financing scale from credit deterioration.

The Bank of England’s July 30 meeting must address both the oil shock and quantitative tightening. No policy-rate change is widely expected, but a minority could support an increase. The bank’s updated balance-sheet analysis will show whether officials are prepared to reduce active gilt sales when maintaining the current overall runoff pace could require those sales to double. For the long end, the QT signal may be as important as the rate vote.

The Bank of Japan follows on July 31. A hold at 1% is expected, but the yen near a 4-decade low and the 40-year yield above 4% have raised the cost of a patient message. Guidance on currency pass-through, energy prices and the timing of the next increase will determine whether the market maintains its expectation of about 32 basis points of tightening by year-end or moves closer to the December timetable favored by economists.

Euro-area GDP and inflation releases will begin building the case for the ECB’s September 10 decision. Economists expect Q2 growth of 0.2% and July inflation of 2.9%. Those forecasts would describe resilient activity and faster price growth, but the more consequential issue is whether energy enters services, wages and medium-term expectations. The June decline in consumer expectations gives the ECB a favorable baseline; it does not answer how households and firms respond to the July shock.

China’s Politburo meeting will test whether policymakers accelerate the 6.8 trillion yuan of remaining bond issuance and improve delivery of existing fiscal support. A faster spending schedule would support activity without requiring a repeat of the 2024 stimulus package. The first repo-linked bank loans add a parallel question: whether more flexible benchmarks can transmit low interbank rates into the real economy when credit demand itself remains weak.

Across these events, the bond market is separating temporary price relief from persistent financing pressure. Lower oil can remove some near-term inflation compensation, as Friday’s breakeven decline demonstrated. It cannot by itself reduce high real yields, absorb long sovereign and AI-related supply, or resolve the fiscal and policy constraints keeping U.S., U.K. and Japanese long yields elevated.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries steady as oil retreats, while real yields and long-end pressure persist
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied modestly as crude retreated from the week’s peak. The 2-year yield fell 1.5 basis points to 4.333%, the 5-year declined 2.7 basis points to 4.426% and the 10-year eased 1.6 basis points to 4.678%, while the 30-year slipped only 0.2 basis point to 5.159%. Brent settled 3.88% lower at $96.78 after briefly exceeding $100, reducing immediate inflation pressure without reversing a week in which Treasury yields and oil rose sharply.

The composition of the move showed why the relief remained limited. The 10-year breakeven fell 2.4 basis points to 2.246%, but the 10-year real yield increased 0.8 basis point to 2.432%. Investors removed some oil-related inflation compensation while continuing to demand a high inflation-adjusted return, and the long bond retained pressure from fiscal supply and growing corporate duration.

U.S. business activity expanded at its fastest pace in 8 months as services offset weaker manufacturing, and new-home sales rose. The data gave the Fed little evidence that growth was weakening enough to disregard energy and tariff risks. Broad equities held steady, but the Nasdaq 100 and semiconductor shares fell as weak demand for long-dated AI financing exposed mounting supply and concentration pressure in investment-grade credit.
overall_summary.summary: Crude’s retreat from above $100 gave Treasuries a modest reprieve, but the 30-year yield barely fell and the 10-year real yield rose, leaving the week’s oil-driven selloff, resilient U.S. activity and mounting long-duration financing pressure largely intact.
